---
title: "Issue triage"
description: "A first look at new issues: one category and a short reason, as a comment."
---

`issue-triage.yml` takes a first look at each new issue, so you can see at
a glance what it is. Claude reads the issue once and picks a category;
the workflow posts one comment with that category, a one-sentence summary
and the reason, and sets the category's label. It never closes an issue.
You decide what happens next.

| Category | Label |
|---|---|
| Bug | `bug` |
| Idea | `enhancement` |
| Question | `question` |
| Duplicate | `duplicate` |
| More information needed | `needs-info` |
| Out of scope | `out-of-scope` |
| Spam | `invalid` |

The labels are set in `config/issue-triage.yml`. When a later triage
reaches another verdict, its label replaces the earlier one; labels people
added stay.

- **It waits for a quiet issue.** People often fix an issue just after
  posting it, so the run waits `wait-minutes` first. Each edit restarts
  the wait, and triage reads the text as it stands at the end.
- **One triage per issue, unless someone answers it.** A later triage
  needs a reason, as below, and there are at most `max-triages` comments
  per issue. Each one restarts the wait, so several replies give one
  triage. It reads the earlier verdict and the comments since.

  | Last verdict | Starts another triage |
  |---|---|
  | More information needed | An edit, or any person's comment |
  | Duplicate, spam, out of scope | A comment by the issue's author, who may disagree |
  | Bug, idea, question | Nothing |

  Before the first triage, comments start nothing; it reads them anyway.
- **What is left alone:** closed issues, issues written by a bot,
  `bot-created` issues, and issues that already carry `approval-label`.

## Example

{{< example issue-triage.yml >}}

The caller has to be on the **default branch**, because `issues` and
`issue_comment` events only start workflows from there. Every issue comment
starts a short run, which ends in seconds if there's nothing to do. A real
triage holds a runner during the wait, which counts as Actions minutes in
private repositories.

The workflow needs [Claude access](claude-setup.qmd): its own federation
rule for `issue-triage.yml`, set up like the others. A separate workspace
gives triage its own spend limit, which helps because anyone who can open
an issue can start a run.

## Issue text is untrusted

Anyone can write anything into an issue or comment, including instructions
aimed at Claude. So the text only reaches Claude, Claude can only answer in fixed
fields, and everything it writes is reduced to plain text before it is
posted: no mentions, links, images or markup. A duplicate is only named if
it is one of the open issues Claude was shown. Labels come from the fixed
list above, and triage refuses to set `approval-label`. At worst, a crafted
issue gets the wrong category and label.
